## Start with a specific question

**LeetCode 28 — Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String.** We will reason from a very small example rather than introduce a complicated notation first.

## What the obvious approach overlooks

For each text position, compare every pattern character again. On repeated prefixes this restarts work that already established partial agreement.

## One simple idea

The KMP prefix function records the longest proper prefix of the pattern that is also a suffix of what was matched. After a mismatch, move the PATTERN state without moving the text backwards.

Before reading symbols, explain the intended operation aloud. If you can say which information is saved and which work is avoided, you have the core intuition.

## Formula and immediate translation

$$
\pi[i]=\max\{k<i+1:P[0:k]=P[i-k+1:i+1]\}
$$

**Symbols and notation:** P is the pattern; i is its current zero-based position; π[i] is the length k of the longest proper prefix equal to a suffix of P's prefix ending at i. Ranges use half-open indexing.

**Insert actual numbers:** For pattern 'abab', prefix ending at index 3 is 'abab'. Its proper prefix 'ab' equals its suffix 'ab', so π[3]=2. On mismatch after matching 'abab', continue with 2 previously matched characters instead of restarting from zero.

This numerical calculation is essential: the expression must mean the same thing when evaluated by hand and when written in code.

## Why the mathematics leads to an algorithm

The already-read text suffix is known to equal a pattern prefix. Other shorter candidates have been excluded, so falling back to π retains the longest possible useful progress.

This argument is the bridge between 'the equation looks plausible' and 'the result is correct for all inputs satisfying the assumptions'.

## Make the idea executable

The [original algorithm examples](../examples/patterns.mjs) provide a small runnable related operation:

~~~js
import { kmpFind } from '../examples/patterns.mjs';

console.log(kmpFind('ababcabc','abc'));
~~~

Run from a saved `.mjs` file inside this topic directory. The exported operation is tested with Node's standard test runner. Some examples illustrate a prerequisite rather than the entire specialised algorithm; in that case, the mathematical model above remains the definition of the full task.

## Complexity and correctness boundaries

**Work bound:** O(n+m) time and O(m) prefix-table space for text length n and pattern length m.

**Counterexample or limitation:** KMP relies on exact symbol equality and matching semantics. Unicode grapheme segmentation, case folding or normalisation need to be handled consistently outside the core algorithm.

Always declare the input domain first. For example, a modulus must be positive, a probability denominator nonzero and a character indexing convention fixed. Many seemingly clever solutions fail because these conditions were never stated.
